package_info.package_versions: N/A (endpoint-based vulnerability, not a software package version)
package_info.why_malicious: The gamma endpoint for AWS Service Catalog allowed both read and write API actions to be performed without generating CloudTrail logs. This enabled attackers with valid credentials to perform unauthorized or stealthy modifications to AWS resources, bypassing standard audit and detection mechanisms.

required_permissions: IAM permissions for Service Catalog actions

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST https://aws242-servicecatalog-gamma.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
Action: servicecatalog:ListPortfolios
(Signature: AWS SIGv4, using valid IAM credentials)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends a signed ListPortfolios request to the gamma Service Catalog endpoint, retrieves portfolio data, and receives results without generating a CloudTrail log entry.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows an attacker to enumerate Service Catalog resources without any trace in CloudTrail, bypassing standard AWS auditing.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, all AWS API calls (including read actions) are logged in CloudTrail for auditing and detection. Here, the action is invisible to defenders.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be normal ListPortfolios calls to the standard endpoint, which are logged.
key_indicators: Absence of CloudTrail logs for API activity
Valid IAM credentials used for stealthy enumeration

required_permissions: IAM permissions for Service Catalog write actions

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST https://aws242-servicecatalog-gamma.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
Action: servicecatalog:CreatePortfolio
Payload: {"ProviderName":"my-provider","DisplayName":"This was made while bypassing CloudTrail","IdempotencyToken":"blahblahblah"}
(Signature: AWS SIGv4, using valid IAM credentials)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends a signed CreatePortfolio request to the gamma Service Catalog endpoint, creates a new portfolio, and receives an error response, but the action completes successfully and is not logged in CloudTrail.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This enables attackers to make unauthorized changes to AWS resources without detection, as the write action is not logged.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Write actions in AWS are always expected to be logged in CloudTrail for accountability. Here, the action is both successful and invisible.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be creating portfolios via the standard endpoint, which is logged.
key_indicators: Write action (CreatePortfolio) not logged in CloudTrail
Error response despite successful resource creation

required_permissions: IAM permissions for Service Catalog write actions

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST https://aws242-servicecatalog-gamma.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
Action: servicecatalog:UpdatePortfolio
Payload: { ... }
(Signature: AWS SIGv4, using valid IAM credentials)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends a signed UpdatePortfolio request to the gamma Service Catalog endpoint, updates an existing portfolio, receives an error response, but the update is applied and not logged in CloudTrail.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Attackers can alter existing AWS resources without detection, as the update action is not logged.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Update actions should always be logged for traceability. Here, the action is both effective and invisible.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be updating portfolios via the standard endpoint, which is logged.
key_indicators: Update action (UpdatePortfolio) not logged in CloudTrail
Error response despite successful resource update

required_permissions: IAM permissions for Control Tower actions

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST https://prod.us-east-1.blackbeard.aws.a2z.com
Action: controltower:ListManagedOrganizationalUnits
(Signature: AWS SIGv4, using valid IAM credentials with insufficient permissions)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends a signed ListManagedOrganizationalUnits request to the Control Tower endpoint with insufficient permissions, receives an error, and the failed action is not logged in CloudTrail.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Attackers can enumerate permissions by brute-forcing API calls without generating failure logs, evading detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Failed API calls due to insufficient permissions are expected to be logged in CloudTrail for monitoring and investigation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be failed calls logged for audit purposes.
key_indicators: Absence of CloudTrail logs for failed API calls

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains valid IAM credentials with sufficient Service Catalog or Control Tower permissions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to interact with AWS APIs

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends signed API requests to the non-standard gamma endpoint for Service Catalog (aws242-servicecatalog-gamma.us-east-1.amazonaws.com) to enumerate or modify resources.
attack_chain.leads_to: Stealthy enumeration and modification of AWS resources without CloudTrail logs

attack_chain.action: Attacker optionally uses the AWSBlackbeardService endpoint to enumerate Control Tower permissions, with failed attempts not being logged.
Attacker achieves persistence or further compromise, undetected due to lack of CloudTrail logging.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: undetected resource modification or privilege escalation

behavioral_signatures: API calls to non-standard AWS endpoints (e.g., gamma, beta, alpha subdomains)
Successful resource creation or modification despite error responses
Absence of expected CloudTrail logs for known API activity
Brute-force enumeration of permissions without corresponding failure logs
file_indicators: N/A (endpoint-based, but logs may show references to aws242-servicecatalog-gamma.us-east-1.amazonaws.com or prod/gamma.us-east-1.blackbeard.aws.a2z.com)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for API calls to non-standard AWS endpoints (such as those containing 'gamma', 'beta', or 'alpha' in the subdomain) in VPC flow logs, DNS logs, or proxy logs. Correlate resource changes in AWS with the absence of corresponding CloudTrail logs. Investigate error responses from AWS APIs that nevertheless result in resource changes. Alert on brute-force permission enumeration attempts where failed API calls are not logged as expected.
